To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cocoon, and the jet, can inhibit the formation of stars within a nearby cloud, and that this inhibition is maintained over long periods of time.

1) the cocoon’s impact on the cloud is determined by the jet’s input power; 2) the cloud’s density is increased and its mass decreased by the jet’s action; 3) the cloud becomes more filamentary, when the jet turns off; 4) star formation is inhibited during the jet active phase; 5) the star formation rate is also inhibited during the passive phase; 6) the star formation from the cloud fragments is strongly inhibited.

(1) the jet cocoon can compress the cloud to a degree that is dependent on the jet power; (2) the jet cocion can strip away the outer layers of the cloud, and (3) the cloud fragments into small clumps.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the interaction between the jet and the cloud, which is the main ingredient of our model for AGN feedback, and the results obtained here are crucial in order to understand the impact of AGN jet feedback in galaxies.
the interaction of an AGN jet with a dense cloud.
the interaction of a jet with the ISM/IGM and its impact on the star forming properties of the ISM/ISM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the range of parameters considered here, the jet-induced cocoon is a powerful mechanism which can suppress star formation, and that this suppression can be long lasting.
the jet has a strong negative impact on the star-formation process, and this effect is long-lasting, as long as the jet is fed.

the AGN jet-induced feedback can be effective in suppressing star formation, even when the jet is active, but the effect is most effective during the passive phase, when the cloud is subject to a back-flow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the context of AGN jet feedback, the cloud’s evolution is dominated by its interaction with the cocoon.
, in general, AGN jet-induced feedback can be effective in suppressing star formation within the cloud.

, in the presence of an AGN jet, the star formation within the dense cloud is suppressed for a time scale comparable to the jet lifetime, and that the jet-induced feedback mechanism can be effective in suppressing star formation in galaxies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AGN jet-induced feedback can be an effective mechanism for quenching star formation in dense clouds, and thus in galaxies.
the star formation within a cloud can be inhibited by the jet-induced feedback, and that this suppression of star formation is not temporary, but rather can last for a long time.
the jet-induced feedback can strongly affect the evolution of a nearby dense cloud, and suppress its star formation rate.
